notes:
One hermes session (`hermes chat` REPL) and one claudecode session driven concurrently in the SAME cwd by run-cell-multi.sh, observed by a single --record daemon. The two transports are disjoint at every layer the daemon keys on: hermes matches on a CommandPattern over the full command line and lives in a ProcessOwnedStore ($HERMES_HOME/state.db, cursored per sessions.id — never per cwd), while claudecode matches ExactName{claude} and lives in FilesUnderRoot{~/.claude/projects}. So the workspace events.jsonl carries two distinct sessions, each with its own working->ready arc and no cross-contamination. This spec is adapter-agnostic: agentA is whichever session enters working first, agentB the other; it mirrors the claudecode/codex template for this scenario. Every phase anchors on a WORKING transition, never a ready, because BOTH adapters emit a transient proc-<PID> pre-session born in ready that never works — anchoring on working skips those placeholders, and new_session on agentB skips agentA's already-matched session. That anchoring matters more for hermes than for its siblings: its `sessions` row is INSERTed only on the first user message, so its ready birth comes from the pre-session, and the shared-workspace pre-session sweep (cleanupPreSessionsForProject matches proc-<PID> rows on projectDir alone, without comparing adapter) can retire it when the partner's real session arrives first. No observations block is asserted: replay's summary reads tokens/cost from the parser fold, and hermes keeps usage on the `sessions` aggregate that only ComputeMetrics reads, so a hermes golden's token/cost vector is structurally zero until a store-derived opt-in exists. Asserts: two distinct sessions, each an independent working->ready arc, in one workspace.

RECORD-TIME FINDINGS (2026-08-03, recording 4-2 via run-cell-multi.sh on daemon aef737b, coexist daemon on :7838, partner=claudecode 2.1.220): 4/4 phases green on the first take.
(1) The scenario's own acceptance criteria are met. One `hermes chat` and one `claude` ran concurrently in ONE shared cwd under a single --record daemon. Each session carries its correct adapter label (hermes 20260803_011105_d40f63 via the store poller; claude-code 8b9025f8-5346-484e-89a6-41e991602e47 via the ~/.claude/projects fswatcher), each has its own independent working->ready arc (hermes 01:11:10.91 -> 01:11:18.93; claude-code 01:11:53.83 -> 01:11:57.59), and no transition on one is attributed to the other. Disjoint transports, disjoint keying, no flapping.
(2) CAVEAT DISCOVERED, and it refutes one line of the assessed recipe: THE HERMES SESSION GOT NO WORKSPACE BINDING IN THE CROSS-ADAPTER RUN. Its transcript_new carries project_dir=null and cwd=null, so the two rows do NOT land under a common workspace slug - only the claudecode row does. The recipe's verify[] asserted "both keyed to the same cwd slug" and its setup asserted that a different-adapter partner leaves exactly one live hermes process so defaultLiveCWD binds it; the recording shows otherwise. This is specific to the cross-adapter run: all three single-agent hermes recordings checked (3-2, 2-7, 2-10) bind their store-keyed session to project_dir="cwd". Also specific to it, and probably related: NO hermes proc-<PID> presession was minted at all here, whereas every single-agent hermes recording has one - the only presession in this recording, proc-45836, is labeled claude-code and reconciles into the claudecode session. MECHANISM UNVERIFIED: the plausible reading is that the claudecode process was scanned and claimed the shared cwd at 01:11:06, ~4s before hermes' TUI finished booting, and hermes never got a presession or a live-process CWD of its own. I did not confirm that from the daemon (its log for this run is empty) - treat it as a hypothesis, not a finding.
(3) THE PILLAR VERDICTS ARE UNCHANGED by (2). 4.2's acceptance criteria are "each session appears with its correct adapter label / states transition independently / no cross-contamination of metrics, parent linkage, or subagent counts / final state ready" - none of which mention the workspace slug, and all four hold. The binding gap is a project-attribution caveat (which project folder the dashboard files the hermes row under), the same class of caveat the 3.2 cell already carries, not a failure of what this cell asserts.
(4) The prompt was WIDENED BEFORE RECORDING per the column's TIMING prerequisite: the assessed "Reply with exactly the word: omega" is a sub-second turn the 2s store poll can commit whole, erasing the ready->working edge that whichever of agentA/agentB resolves to hermes needs. It now asks for 120 lines plus two sentences - still tool-free, still no waiting. The hermes turn ran 8.0s.
(5) The assessed setup note telling record to "port opencode's store-export step so it writes a real JSONL before running the rig" was STALE and has been dropped: export_transcript/export_all_transcripts already live in the hermes driver, as the 17 committed hermes recordings with real transcripts and goldens show.
(6) observations: `model` PINNED (it is readable from the replay golden). tokens/cost stay unpinned for the standing hermes-column reason - `of verify` asserts against the replay-golden summary and hermes' replay path runs Parser, not ComputeMetrics over the store, so the token aggregate is 0 by construction.

text: First agent's turn drives ready -> working (binds agentA; skips both adapters' born-ready proc-<PID> placeholders by anchoring on working)
First agent's turn completes: working -> ready
The OTHER agent (a DISTINCT session, different adapter, same cwd) drives ready -> working independently (new_session proves it is not agentA; working anchor skips the placeholders)
Second agent's turn completes: working -> ready — two agents, one workspace, labeled independently with no cross-contamination
